problem: Directly training MARL policies for multi-agent navigation has low data efficiency in large search spaces (many agents, complex environments), and existing goal-conditioned HRL assigns subgoals that only implicitly relate to the true target goals, confusing agents.
motivation: Multi-agent navigation is used in logistics, driving and rescue, but MARL baselines only work with few agents. Assigning true target goals in a high-level policy turns the task into several single-agent navigation problems, and a GNN in the low-level policy can improve cooperation and collision avoidance.
key_idea: A hierarchical framework where a high-level Goal Commander assigns each agent a target goal (trained with a Hungarian-algorithm-relative reward) and a low-level graph-based Action Executor uses a learned sparse subgraph of teammates plus a goal encoder to act.
insight: Assigning real target goals instead of abstract subgoals makes the low-level problem a goal-conditioned single-agent task, which gives large gains in data efficiency. Ablations on Simple Spread with 50 agents: random goal assignment gives 0.83 SR, an attention module instead of the Gumbel-softmax subgraph gives 0.93, and an MLP executor gives 0.50, versus 1.00 for the full model. Selecting only crucial neighbors helps more than attending to all teammates, and the executor needs explicit graph and goal modeling.
method: Goal Scheduler (Goal Commander): an MLP takes all agent and goal positions, applies softmax to get a goal probability distribution, ranks goals and assigns them in order to agents. It acts once per episode and is trained with reward R_c = 1 - C_c/C_h (assignment distance cost vs. the Hungarian algorithm).

Subgraph Extractor: an MLP observation encoder and GCN over a fully connected agent graph, then a Gumbel-softmax over MLP-updated features gives a sparse adjacency matrix. A second GCN produces each agent's subgraph feature over its crucial neighbors (l_g=2 blocks).
Goal Encoder: an MLP encodes the agent's own observation together with its assigned goal position.
State Extractor: concatenates the goal embedding and subgraph feature, passes them through an MLP and an RNN to give goal-guided team representation E_all.
Action Generator: outputs a discrete primitive action per agent from E_all. Environment reward is a linear combination of completion bonus, distance penalty and collision penalty.
Training: Commander and Executor are trained separately with MAPPO, using separate buffers. The Commander is centralized (CTCE) and Executors are decentralized with partial observation.

setting.backbone: MLP + GCN + Gumbel-softmax + RNN policies trained with MAPPO (from scratch)
setting.training_data: online RL in MPE (Simple Spread, Push Ball) and gym-pybullet-drones; about 3M steps for 50 agents in Simple Spread; 3 seeds
setting.observation: agent's own position, assigned goal position, other agents' positions, and a reached-goal one-hot (state vectors, no images)
setting.action_space: discrete: Up/Down/Left/Right in MPE; per-axis acceleration direction (Forward/Backward/Stop) for drones
setting.privileged: Goal Commander uses all agent positions and goal positions (centralized); Hungarian algorithm used as a training reward only

Table 3: 4 agents Suc. Rate 0.79(0.07), Colli. Rate 0.12(0.01)

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN/ObjNav benchmark; results are on custom MPE and drone multi-agent tasks. Values are means over 300 test episodes; SR converted from fractions to percent. Baseline numbers were excluded.
results: MAGE-X reaches 100% SR in Simple Spread with 5/20/50 agents (best baseline in 50 agents: MAPPO 0.13) and in Push Ball with 5/20 agents (baselines at most 0.36). In drones it achieves 0.95 and 0.79 SR, beating MAPPO's 0.83 and 0.64, with about 2x sample efficiency in the 4-agent case.
limitations: Only evaluated on simple state-based multi-agent navigation, with no visual observations, real robots or realistic maps.
The Goal Commander assigns goals once at the start, so it cannot reassign goals dynamically, and it needs global positions of all agents and goals.
In the 4-drone task the collision rate (0.12) is not the lowest (MAT 0.06, DICG 0.07).
